doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: Steering by the Stars and Trio Globo
summary: Levy tells how a book on Polynesian navigation inspired Steering by the Stars, and how Trio Globo works as three equals.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Speaking of Trio Globo I wanted to compliment you on the tune “Steering by the Stars.”
And I don't know if it put it in my head but I got this nautical images from that song.

Absolutely. I was on the road with the Flecktones and I went to a bookstore and got out a book that I still remember the name of, my goodness. It was called Song for Satawal and it went into great detail about how Polynesians navigated these vast distances traversing the Pacific Ocean making star charts out of like cane and pebbles. And they would sight these stars through these charts and also feel the direction of the currents with their bodies as they sailed with no maps across hundreds and hundreds of miles of ocean. And this inspired me to write “Steering by the Stars.” You nailed it. And I wrote it, I used a carry a little keyboard with me and we were staying in a little like bunch of cabins on the Pacific Ocean near San Diego and I wrote that in my hotel room there. And it took quite a few years for me to – well I guess, yeah, we recorded that in like maybe 2008 or something like that. It took almost fifteen years to record that after I wrote it. Yeah. Wow.
These projects that you do, do you get the idea and then look for the people, or do you hear other musicians who inspire the idea?

Both. Definitely. I mean with Trio Globo, Gene and Glen are very inspiring players and composers, and so that group is a very – it’s like a group of three equals and we all are inspired by each other and write things for each other. And then sometimes I just, you know, write a tune and say, “Could you guys do this?” And sometimes they say no and
sometimes they say yes. And whenever they say yes it ends up sounding way better than anything I could have imagined.
